newsitem.title: CHINA: Official Chinese agency backs down on news fees.
newsitem.headline: Official Chinese agency backs down on news fees.

text.p: China's official Xinhua news agency said on Friday it had withdrawn a plan to impose a fee on foreign financial news organisations but would supervise their activities.
A Xinhua official told Reuters that the management fee, part of sweeping controls issued in the name of state security early last year, would not be applied.
The official said news agencies had already been informed and that all other provisions of the regulations would be enforced.

China ordered all foreign news agencies to submit to regulation by the Communist Party-directed Xinhua news agency, which was given exclusive management over foreign news agencies and their subsidiary organisations.
The edict, which threatened punishment for news vendors whose information "slanders" China, banned domestic organisations from directly buying economic information from foreign sources.
It also allowed Xinhua to determine subscription rates.
Xinhua had distributed general news but economic information had long been made available directly to customers in China.
The edict was widely criticised by foreign news organisations as well as Western government officials as a restriction on the free flow of economic information.
Western trade officials had also maintained the monopoly was a violation of China's commitment to liberalise access to its market as part of its plan to join the World Trade Organisation.
U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan raised the issue of curbs on economic news in talks with Chinese officials during a visit to Beijing this week, sources close to the discussions said.
Greenspan was quoted as telling State Planning Commission chief Chen Jinhua of the importance of the free flow of information to the development of financial markets.
Foreign news organisations in China include Reuters Holdings Plc, Dow Jones and Co Inc and Bloomberg.
